A description of a stack: its layers in order, each with its output width and its activation,
from inputs tagged `i` to outputs tagged `o`.

One is started with `input` and extended with `dense` and `denseTo`. `o` is `i` while there is no
layer, `Width` when the last layer was added by `dense`, and the `Dim`'s tag when it was added by
`denseTo`. The input width is not part of a description; `params` takes it.

unions.name: Stack
unions.comment:
The layers of a stack of dtype `d`, from inputs tagged `i` to outputs tagged `o`: each layer's
weight, bias and activation. A value is made by the `Param.Spec` that `params` returns, from the
tensors that spec is given. Given fewer tensors than the spec has fields, it holds fewer layers than
the `Seq` that `params` was given.

unions.name: Width
unions.comment:
The tag of the outputs of a layer added by `dense`, standing for whatever width `dense` gave
that layer.

No value of this type can be made, so `Tensor.dim` cannot make a `Dim Width`.

values.name: apply
values.comment:
Returns each row passed through the stack's layers in order: each multiplies it by its weight,
adds its bias and applies its activation. A stack with no layers returns the rows unchanged; rows
whose width differs from the first layer's input width are a build error.
values.type: Nn.Stack.Stack d i o -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 n i) -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 n o)

values.name: applyWithDropout
values.comment:
Returns the rows passed through the stack as `apply` does, with dropout applied to the output of
every layer but the last, whether `dense` or `denseTo` added it. The output of layer k, counting
from 0, is passed through `Nn.dropout` with the given `rate` and `training` and the seed
`Tensor.Random.salt k seed`. When `training` is False or `rate` is 0 or less, the result is
`apply`'s.
values.type: { rate : Basics.Float, training : Basics.Bool } -> Tensor.Random.Seed -> Nn.Stack.Stack d i o -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 n i) -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 n o)

values.name: dense
values.comment:
Returns the description with a layer added after its last one: a layer of `n` outputs, tagged
`Width`, and activation `act`. Nothing in this module checks `n`, so a width of 0 or less is
accepted.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Nn.Stack.Activation -> Nn.Stack.Seq i o -> Nn.Stack.Seq i Nn.Stack.Width

values.name: denseTo
values.comment:
Returns the description with a layer added after its last one. The added layer's output width is
the size of the given `Dim`, and its outputs carry that `Dim`'s tag. It can add any layer, not only
the last.
values.type: Tensor.Dim o2 -> Nn.Stack.Activation -> Nn.Stack.Seq i o -> Nn.Stack.Seq i o2

values.name: gelu
values.comment: The activation that `Tensor.gelu` computes: the erf form of GELU, not its tanh approximation.
values.type: Nn.Stack.Activation

values.name: input
values.comment: The description with no layers. A stack made from it returns its inputs unchanged.
values.type: Nn.Stack.Seq i i

values.name: none
values.comment: No activation: the layer's outputs are x · W + b itself.
values.type: Nn.Stack.Activation

values.name: params
values.comment:
Returns the parameter description of the stack the `Seq` describes, of the given dtype, whose
first layer reads inputs of the width the `Dim i` gives.

Its tensor fields are, layer by layer, the weight, of input width × output width, and the bias, of
output width. All are trainable. A weight's first values are drawn as `Param.heUniform` describes,
and a bias's first values are zeros. Built from fewer tensors than it has fields, the stack has
only the layers whose weight and bias were both given; no missing tensor is filled in.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float d -> Tensor.Dim i -> Nn.Stack.Seq i o -> Param.Spec (Nn.Stack.Stack d i o)

values.name: relu
values.comment: The activation that `Tensor.relu` computes: each element, or 0 where it is below 0.
values.type: Nn.Stack.Activation

name: Nn.Transformer
comment:
This module builds the two kinds of layer in a transformer, an encoder layer and a decoder
layer, from attention (`Nn.Attention`), layer normalisation (`Nn.LayerNorm`) and dense layers
(`Nn.Linear`). For each kind it provides the parameter record, a description of that record for
`Param`, and the function that applies it.

A layer reads a sequence `x` of `s` positions, each a row of `m` features (the _model width_), and
returns a sequence of the same shape. It is made of _blocks_, each of which computes something from
the sequence and adds it to the sequence. Adding a block's output to its input is the _residual_
connection, and the sum is the sequence the next block reads. An encoder layer has two blocks:
self-attention, in which the positions of `x` attend to one another (each only to itself and the
positions before it, if `encode` asks for that), and then a feed-forward block. A decoder layer has
three: self-attention in which each position attends only to itself and the positions before it,
attention from `x` to a second sequence, the _memory_, and then the feed-forward block.

The layers are _pre-norm_: each block normalises its input with its own layer normalisation before
computing from it, and its output is added to the input as it was before normalising. A layer's
result is that sum, and is not normalised.

The feed-forward block maps each row from `m` features to `f` with one dense layer, applies GELU to
each element as `Tensor.gelu` computes it, and maps the row back to `m` features with a second dense
layer. The attention blocks are those of `Nn.Attention`, with `h` heads of `j` features;
`Nn.Attention` says when a model width that is not h × j is a build error.

Each block's output passes through dropout (`Nn.dropout`) before it is added, at the rate in the
layer's `dropout` field. Nothing else in a layer is dropped: not the attention weights, and not the
feed-forward block's `f` features. The function that applies a layer takes one seed and draws each
block's mask on that seed salted (`Tensor.Random.salt`) with the block's position: 0, 1 and, in a
decoder layer, 2. Two layers given one seed therefore draw their masks on the same seeds.

In the types, `d` is the dtype, `m` the model width, `h` the number of heads, `j` the features of
a head, `f` the width of the feed-forward block, `s` the number of positions of `x` and `t` the
number of positions of the memory.


# Layers

@docs EncoderLayer, DecoderLayer, encoderParams, decoderParams


# Applying

@docs encode, decode

aliases.name: DecoderLayer
aliases.comment:
The parameters of one decoder layer.

`self` holds the self-attention block's attention parameters and `cross` those of the attention to
the memory. Both are an `Attention d m h j`, so the memory has `m` features, like the input.
`norm1`, `norm2` and `norm3` normalise the inputs of the self-attention, the attention to the memory
and the feed-forward block, in that order. `up`, `down` and `dropout` are as in `EncoderLayer`.
aliases.type: { norm1 : Nn.LayerNorm.LayerNorm d m, self : Nn.Attention.Attention d m h j, norm2 : Nn.LayerNorm.LayerNorm d m, cross : Nn.Attention.Attention d m h j, norm3 : Nn.LayerNorm.LayerNorm d m, up : Nn.Linear.Linear d m f, down : Nn.Linear.Linear d f m, dropout : Basics.Float }

aliases.name: EncoderLayer
aliases.comment:
The parameters of one encoder layer.

`norm1` normalises the input of the self-attention block and `norm2` that of the feed-forward
block, whose two dense layers are `up`, from `m` features to `f`, and `down`, from `f` back to `m`.
`dropout` is the rate `Nn.dropout` is given for every block: for a rate between 0 and 1, the
probability that each element of a block's output is dropped while training.
aliases.type: { norm1 : Nn.LayerNorm.LayerNorm d m, attention : Nn.Attention.Attention d m h j, norm2 : Nn.LayerNorm.LayerNorm d m, up : Nn.Linear.Linear d m f, down : Nn.Linear.Linear d f m, dropout : Basics.Float }

values.name: decode
values.comment:
Returns `x` after the decoder layer `p`, which attends to `memory`, a sequence of `t` positions
of `m` features:

    h1 =
        x + dropout (self (norm1 x))

    h2 =
        h1 + dropout (cross memory (norm2 h1))

    result =
        h2 + dropout (down (gelu (up (norm3 h2))))

In the self-attention each position attends only to itself and the positions before it. In the
attention to `memory` every position of `x` attends to every position of `memory`, which is used
as given: the layer does not normalise it. The three dropouts draw on `seed` salted with 0, 1
and 2. With `training` False nothing is dropped and the result does not depend on `seed`.
values.type: { training : Basics.Bool } -> Tensor.Random.Seed -> Nn.Transformer.DecoderLayer d m h j f -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 t m) -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 s m) -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 s m)

values.name: decoderParams
values.comment:
Returns the description of a `DecoderLayer`, made as `encoderParams` makes an encoder layer's,
with both attention blocks described by `Nn.Attention.params`. The tensor fields are those of
`norm1`, `self`, `norm2`, `cross`, `norm3`, `up` and `down`, in that order, and `dropout` is a
config field holding the given rate.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float d -> { model : Tensor.Dim m, heads : Tensor.Dim h, headDim : Tensor.Dim j, feedForward : Tensor.Dim f, dropout : Basics.Float } -> Param.Spec (Nn.Transformer.DecoderLayer d m h j f)

values.name: encode
values.comment:
Returns `x` after the encoder layer `p`:

    h1 =
        x + dropout (attention (norm1 x))

    result =
        h1 + dropout (down (gelu (up (norm2 h1))))

With `causal` True each position attends only to itself and the positions before it, and with it
False every position attends to every position, as `Nn.Attention.self` describes. The two dropouts
draw on `seed` salted with 0 and 1. With `training` False nothing is dropped and the result does
not depend on `seed`.
values.type: { causal : Basics.Bool, training : Basics.Bool } -> Tensor.Random.Seed -> Nn.Transformer.EncoderLayer d m h j f -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 s m) -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R2 s m)

values.name: encoderParams
values.comment:
Returns the description of an `EncoderLayer` of width `model` with `heads` heads of `headDim`
features and a feed-forward block of width `feedForward`.

Each part is described by its own module: the layer normalisations by `Nn.LayerNorm.params`, the
attention by `Nn.Attention.params` and the two dense layers by `Nn.Linear.params`, so every
projection and dense layer has a trainable bias. The tensor fields are those of `norm1`,
`attention`, `norm2`, `up` and `down`, in that order. `dropout` is a config field holding the given
rate, so the rate is part of the description: `Param.config` says where a record holding a
different rate is refused.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float d -> { model : Tensor.Dim m, heads : Tensor.Dim h, headDim : Tensor.Dim j, feedForward : Tensor.Dim f, dropout : Basics.Float } -> Param.Spec (Nn.Transformer.EncoderLayer d m h j f)

name: Optim
comment:
Training moves each trainable parameter against the gradient of the loss, and an optimizer is
the rule that decides how each one moves. This module makes optimizers, namely stochastic gradient
descent (SGD), AdamW and an optimizer with an update written by hand, and can add a bound on the
size of the gradients to an optimizer.

An optimizer is a value, not a graph. `Train.step` applies it when it builds a training graph, to
each trainable parameter separately: the optimizer's _update_ is given one parameter, its gradient
and that parameter's own state, and gives back the parameter's new value and its new state. The one
rule that reads the gradients of all the trainable parameters together is clipping
(`clipGlobalNorm`), which is applied to the gradients before any update.

Three quantities recur. The _learning rate_ is the factor by which the built-in optimizers scale
each move; it is either fixed when the optimizer is made or given with every run of the training
graph (`Rate`). A parameter's _state_ is the tensors an optimizer carries for it from one step to
the next, such as a running average of its gradient. Each of them is a _state slot_: a tensor of the
parameter's shape that is kept between runs in a resident buffer (see `Train`), and that
`Train.initial` and `Train.initialFrom` start at zero. For an optimizer that keeps state, the _step_
(`Hyper`) is one more than the training graph's step counter, which those two functions also start
at zero.

`Train.step` gives an update the parameter, its gradient and its state in f32, whatever the
parameter's dtype, and casts the new parameter back to that dtype.

In the update formulas below, w is a parameter, g its gradient, η the learning rate and t the step.
Every operation in them is element-wise.


# Types

@docs Optimizer, Rate, Hyper


# SGD and AdamW

@docs sgd, sgdWith, adamW, adamWWith


# Your own

`custom` makes an optimizer from an update written with the operations of `Tensor`.

@docs custom


# Clipping

@docs clipGlobalNorm

unions.name: Rate
unions.comment:
Where an optimizer's learning rate comes from.

`Fixed` carries the rate, which is written into the training graph as a constant, so a different
rate needs a new graph.

`PerStep` makes the rate an input of the training graph, fed with every run, so that it can change
from one run to the next, as a schedule needs. `Train.step` describes that input, `rate`.

aliases.name: Hyper
aliases.comment:
What a `custom` update is given besides one parameter's tensors: the learning rate and the step,
each an f32 scalar.

`rate` is the fixed rate or the run's `rate` input, as `Rate` says. When the optimizer has state
slots, `step` is one more than the training graph's step counter, which `Train.initial` and
`Train.initialFrom` start at zero. An optimizer with none has no counter, and its `step` is 1 on
every step. `Train.step` describes the counter.
aliases.type: { rate : Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.R0, step : Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.R0 }

aliases.name: Optimizer
aliases.comment:
A rule for updating the trainable parameters of a model in training, together with where its
learning rate comes from, how many state slots it keeps for each trainable parameter, and whether it
clips the gradients.

The functions of this module are the only way to make one, and `Train.step` is what applies it.

values.name: adamW
values.comment:
Returns the optimizer `adamWWith` gives at the fixed rate `rate`, with β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999,
ε = 10⁻⁸, bias correction, and no weight decay, which makes it Adam.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Optim.Optimizer

values.name: adamWWith
values.comment:
Returns AdamW. Its two state slots, m and v, are running averages of the gradient and of its
square:

    m ← β₁m + (1 − β₁)g
    v ← β₂v + (1 − β₂)g²
    w ← w − η (m̂ / (√v̂ + ε) + λw)

where β₁ = `beta1`, β₂ = `beta2`, ε = `epsilon` and λ = `weightDecay`. With `biasCorrection`,
m̂ = m / (1 − β₁ᵗ) and v̂ = v / (1 − β₂ᵗ); without it, m̂ = m and v̂ = v. The weight decay is not
added to the gradient, so it does not pass through m and v, but it is still scaled by η.

The graph computes βᵗ as exp(t ln β), so with bias correction a negative β gives NaN.
values.type: { rate : Optim.Rate, beta1 : Basics.Float, beta2 : Basics.Float, epsilon : Basics.Float, weightDecay : Basics.Float, biasCorrection : Basics.Bool } -> Optim.Optimizer

values.name: clipGlobalNorm
values.comment:
Returns the optimizer with its gradients clipped by global norm: before any update, the
gradient of every trainable parameter is multiplied by min(1, `maxNorm` / n), where n is the square
root of the sum of the squares of the elements of all those gradients together, as `Train.step`
describes. A later `clipGlobalNorm` replaces the bound an earlier one set.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Optim.Optimizer -> Optim.Optimizer

values.name: custom
values.comment:
Returns an optimizer at the rate `rate` that, when `slots` is 0 or more, keeps `slots` state
slots for each trainable parameter and moves it by `update`.

The parameter's tensors are typed with `Tensor.Elems`, which stands for whatever shape the parameter
has, so one function serves every parameter; only the operations that accept a tensor of any shape
accept them.

Nothing here checks that `update` gives back as many state tensors as it was given.
values.type: { rate : Optim.Rate, slots : Basics.Int, update : Optim.Hyper -> { param : Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems, grad : Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems, state : List.List (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems) } -> { param : Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems, state : List.List (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems) } } -> Optim.Optimizer

values.name: sgd
values.comment:
Returns stochastic gradient descent at the fixed rate η = `rate`, with no momentum and no weight
decay: w ← w − η g. It keeps no state.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Optim.Optimizer

values.name: sgdWith
values.comment:
Returns stochastic gradient descent with momentum μ = `momentum` and weight decay
λ = `weightDecay`:

    g' = g + λw
    v ← μv + g'
    w ← w − η v

v, the velocity, is the one state slot. A `momentum` of 0 keeps no state, and the parameter moves by
w ← w − η g'. The weight decay is added to the gradient, so with momentum it is accumulated in v as
well.
values.type: { rate : Optim.Rate, momentum : Basics.Float, weightDecay : Basics.Float } -> Optim.Optimizer

name: Param
comment:
A model's parameters are a record of tensors, and several things have to be derived from that
record and agree with one another: the graph inputs that carry it, the names of the buffers that
keep it between runs, its first values and its gradient. This module lets a program describe the
record once, in the style of `elm/json` decoders, and derives each of them from that one
description.

    params =
        Param.record Params
            |> Param.sub .l1 (Linear.params T.float32 pixels hidden)
            |> Param.sub .l2 (Linear.params T.float32 hidden classes)

A _description_ (`Spec r`) lists the record's _tensor fields_ in order, each with a dtype, a shape
and a kind. A part (`sub`, `list`) contributes its own tensor fields at the place where it is added.
That order is the order of everything derived from the description: the slots of `sig`, the names
of `names`, the entries of `initial` and the outputs of the graphs built here. A field's _kind_ says
what training does with it and how it is first filled:

  - a _trainable_ field is updated by training, and its first values are given by its
    _initialiser_, one of those that `heUniform` .. `ones` describe;
  - a _frozen_ field (`frozen`) gets its first values in the same way but is not updated by
    training;
  - a _data_ field (`data`) is not updated by training, and `initial`, `initGraph` and
    `initInPlace` fill it with zeros.

A _config_ field (`config`) is not a parameter. It holds a value fixed by the description, such as a
dimension or a constant tensor, and has no slot, no buffer and no initial value.

A field's values can be kept in a _resident buffer_, which whatever runs a graph keeps from one run
to the next (see `Graph.Role`). Each tensor field has a _resident name_, which `names` gives: the
name of the buffer that holds it. `initial`, `initInPlace` and `importGraph` address a field's
buffer by that name, and so must any graph that is to share it. `sig` and `initGraph` do not: their
slots are `Fed`, and `Graph.build` names them from their labels.

First values are made from a seed in one of two ways: `initial` computes them in Elm and gives them
as bytes, while `initGraph` and `initInPlace` build a graph that draws them with random operations.
The two draw differently, so for one seed a drawn field's values from each need not agree.

The He and Xavier initialisers scale their distribution by a field's _fan-in_ and _fan-out_. A
field is read as a weight whose last axis indexes the outputs: the fan-out is the size of that axis,
and the fan-in is the product of the sizes of the other axes, or 1 where that product is less
than 1. A rank-0 field has a fan-in and a fan-out of 1.

Each of these adds a trainable field, given the accessor that reads it, its dtype and its shape
(see `Field`).

aliases.name: Builder
aliases.comment:
A parameter description being put together, as an `elm/json` decoder pipeline is: `r` is the
type of the record it reads tensors from and `f` the type of what it has built so far.

`record` starts one from the record's constructor, so that `f` is the constructor's type, and each
field function supplies the constructor's next argument together with the accessor that reads that
field back. Once every argument is supplied, `f` is `r` and the builder is a `Spec r`. Each accessor
must read the field its argument fills, which no type checks. When a signature made with `sig` is a
graph's input, `Graph.build` notices, through the round trip, a wrong accessor of a tensor field or
of a part that holds tensor fields; as a graph's output it can miss one.

This is not a `Signature.Builder`: `sig` makes a signature from a complete description.

aliases.name: Field
aliases.comment:
The type of the trainable-field functions (`heUniform` .. `ones`): a function that takes the
accessor that reads a float tensor field from the record, the field's dtype and its shape, and adds
the field to a builder as its next argument.
aliases.type: (r -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s) -> Tensor.DType Basics.Float d -> Tensor.Shape s -> Param.Builder r (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> f) -> Param.Builder r f

aliases.name: Spec
aliases.comment:
A complete description of a parameter record of type `r`: its tensor fields in order, each with
a dtype, a shape and a kind, and the values of its config fields.

values.name: config
values.comment:
Adds a config field: a value that is part of the description, `value`, rather than a parameter,
such as a dimension or a constant tensor. It has no slot, no resident buffer and no initial value,
and `count` does not count it.

Every record built from the description holds `value` in this field, including the records that
`grad` and `mapElems` return. The field is compared with `value`, by `==`, only where `sig` flattens
a record, and the record is refused when they are not equal, so a NaN is refused even when it is
`value`. `importGraph` does not read the field of the record its conversion returns.
values.type: (r -> c) -> c -> Param.Builder r (c -> f) -> Param.Builder r f

values.name: count
values.comment: Returns the number of tensor fields, trainable, frozen and data. Config fields are not counted.
values.type: Param.Spec r -> Basics.Int

values.name: data
values.comment:
Adds a data field: a tensor of any element type, read back by the accessor, with the given dtype
and shape.

Training does not update it, and `initial`, `initGraph` and `initInPlace` give it zeros. Any other
contents have to come from elsewhere, such as `importGraph`.
values.type: (r -> Tensor.Tensor k d s) -> Tensor.DType k d -> Tensor.Shape s -> Param.Builder r (Tensor.Tensor k d s -> f) -> Param.Builder r f

values.name: frozen
values.comment:
Returns the description `s` with every trainable field made frozen: first filled as its
initialiser says, but not updated by training. Data fields are unchanged.

A frozen field's resident name is made from `frozen` instead of `param`, so freezing renames the
fields it changes and can renumber the other fields of their group (see `names`).
values.type: Param.Spec p -> Param.Spec p

values.name: grad
values.comment:
Returns the gradient of `loss` at the record the description builds from `r`'s tensors, as a
record of the same type, holding for each tensor field the gradient with respect to that field.

Frozen and float data fields get a gradient too. A non-float data field, and a field the loss does
not depend on, get zeros. Config fields hold the description's values.
values.type: Param.Spec r -> (r -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d Tensor.R0) -> r -> r

values.name: heNormal
values.comment:
Adds a trainable field whose first values are drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0 and
standard deviation √(2 / fan-in).
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

values.name: heUniform
values.comment:
Adds a trainable field whose first values are drawn uniformly between −b and b, where
b = √(6 / fan-in).
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

values.name: importGraph
values.comment:
Builds the graph `graphName`, which reads raw tensors, such as a checkpoint's, from resident
buffers, converts them with `convert` into a parameter record, and writes every tensor field of
that record into its resident buffer (`names`), whatever its kind.

The raw buffers' names come from the labels of `raw`'s slots: a label used once is the name, a
repeated one is numbered (`w0`, `w1` ..), and an unlabelled slot counts as labelled `raw`. The
numbers are not checked against the other labels, so `w`, `w`, `w1` give two slots the one buffer
`w1`. Each raw slot must declare a dtype and a shape; otherwise the result is an error for each
slot that does not, and no graph is built.

The tensors `convert` gives are paired with the fields in order. Each tensor paired with a field
must have exactly that field's dtype and shape; one that does not carries a build error naming the
field's resident name, so the graph is refused. The lengths of the converted record's `list` parts
are not checked against their `n`: a longer one moves later tensors onto the wrong fields, and
tensors past the last field are dropped unchecked; with fewer tensors than fields, `Graph.build`
refuses the graph with an error that names no field. The config fields of the converted record are
not read.
values.type: String.String -> Param.Spec r -> Signature.Sig raw -> (raw -> r) -> Result.Result (List.List String.String) Graph.Graph

values.name: initGraph
values.comment:
Builds the graph `graphName`, which takes a seed and returns every tensor field's first values,
in field order.

The graph has one fed input, `seed`, a `ui64 [1]` tensor. A drawn field `i`, counting every tensor
field from 0, is drawn from the seed salted as `Tensor.Random.salt i` salts it. Trainable and frozen
fields are drawn as their initialisers say, in `f32` and then cast to the field's dtype; fields
initialised by `zeros` or `ones`, and data fields, are constant fills. The drawn values need not
agree with those `initial` computes for the same seed, and depend on what runs the graph, as
`Tensor.Random` describes.

The outputs are fed. They are labelled by kind, as `sig` labels its slots, so their names are those
`names` gives only if no field is in a `named` part.
values.type: String.String -> Param.Spec r -> Result.Result (List.List String.String) Graph.Graph

values.name: initInPlace
values.comment:
Builds the graph `graphName`, which draws the same values as `initGraph` but gives each as a
resident output rather than a fed one: every output is `Resident` under the field's resident name
(`names`). The outputs' names are those of `initGraph`; only their resident names follow `named`.
values.type: String.String -> Param.Spec r -> Result.Result (List.List String.String) Graph.Graph

values.name: initial
values.comment:
Returns every tensor field's first values, computed in Elm from the seed, in field order, each
as bytes under the field's resident name (`names`).

Trainable and frozen fields are drawn as their initialisers say, and data fields are zeros. The
draws come from the package's own pseudo-random generator, whose state passes from each field to
the next, so a field's values depend on the fields drawn before it. They need not be the values
`initGraph` draws for the same seed. Drawn values need not agree to the last bit across platforms:
those of a normal initialiser for any seed, and any of them for a seed of magnitude beyond about
5.4 · 10⁹.

The bytes are in the encoding stated in `Train`'s module documentation.
values.type: Param.Spec r -> Basics.Int -> List.List ( String.String, Bytes.Bytes )

values.name: list
values.comment:
Returns a description of a list of `n` values, each described by `s`, such as the layers of a
stack. Its tensor fields are those of `s`, repeated `n` times.

For `n` of 0 or more, building gives `n` records. Flattening lists the tensors of every record in
the list it is given, whatever the list's length. `sig` refuses a length other than `n` when it
flattens the list.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Param.Spec p -> Param.Spec (List.List p)

values.name: mapElems
values.comment:
Returns the record the description builds from `r`'s tensors, paired with its tensor fields in
order, after `f` is applied to each tensor paired with a trainable field. Such a tensor is converted
to `f32` for `f` and back to that field's dtype afterwards; the others are kept as they are. Config
fields hold the description's values.
values.type: (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.Elems) -> Param.Spec r -> r -> r

values.name: named
values.comment:
Returns the description `s` with its fields put in the group `n`, so that their resident names
begin with `n.` (see `names`). A group's names depend only on its own fields, so while no field
outside this part is in the group `n`, the names beginning `n.` stay the same wherever the part
sits in a larger description.

Only fields that are in no group yet are moved: the innermost `named` around a field wins, and
names do not nest. `named "a" (named "b" s)` gives `s`'s fields names beginning `b.`; write
`named "a.b"` for that name. Parts given the same name form one group and are numbered together.
values.type: String.String -> Param.Spec p -> Param.Spec p

values.name: names
values.comment:
Returns the resident name of each tensor field, in field order: the name of the buffer that
holds the field between runs, which `initial`, `initInPlace` and `importGraph` use.

A field's name is its kind's label, `param` for a trainable field, `frozen` for a frozen one and
`data` for a data field, numbered among the fields of its group when the label occurs there more
than once. A _group_ is either the fields that carry one name from `named`, whose names begin with
that name and a dot, or the fields that no `named` reaches. So three fields outside any `named`
part, two trainable and then one frozen, are `param0`, `param1` and `frozen`, and the same three
under `named "enc"` are `enc.param0`, `enc.param1` and `enc.frozen`. The names are distinct.

A name depends on the kinds and the order of the other fields in its group, so adding, removing or
freezing a field can rename the others in its group.
values.type: Param.Spec r -> List.List String.String

values.name: normal
values.comment:
Produces the field function for a trainable field whose first values are drawn from a normal
distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation `std`.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Param.Field r d s f

values.name: ones
values.comment: Adds a trainable field whose first values are all 1.
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

values.name: record
values.comment:
Starts a description of a record from its constructor. Each field added after it supplies the
constructor's next argument, in order.
values.type: f -> Param.Builder r f

values.name: sig
values.comment:
Returns the signature of a parameter record: one slot for each tensor field, in field order,
with the field's dtype and shape.

Every slot is `Fed`, so a graph that takes this signature as its input is given the parameters with
every run and keeps no buffer for them. The slots are labelled `param`, `frozen` or `data` by kind,
and `Graph.build` names them as it names any labelled slots, numbering a label that several slots
of the whole signature carry. When no field is in a `named` part, the slots keep these labels and
no other slot of the signature carries one of them, the names are those `names` gives.

When this signature flattens a record that does not match the description, because a config field
holds another value or a `list` has the wrong length, every tensor it lists carries a build error
describing the first mismatch found, prefixed with `Param:`. Built from too few tensors, it makes
each missing field that `heUniform` .. `ones` or `data` added a rank-0 zero of the field's dtype.
values.type: Param.Spec r -> Signature.Sig r

values.name: sub
values.comment:
Adds a field holding a part with its own description, such as a layer's parameters. The part's
tensor fields join this description's at this point, in their own order, and `getter` reads the
part back from the record.
values.type: (r -> p) -> Param.Spec p -> Param.Builder r (p -> f) -> Param.Builder r f

values.name: xavierNormal
values.comment:
Adds a trainable field whose first values are drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0 and
standard deviation √(2 / (fan-in + fan-out)).
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

values.name: xavierUniform
values.comment:
Adds a trainable field whose first values are drawn uniformly between −b and b, where
b = √(6 / (fan-in + fan-out)).
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

values.name: zeros
values.comment: Adds a trainable field whose first values are all 0.
values.type: Param.Field r d s f

name: Signature
comment:
Graphs, transforms and control flow take and give tensors as an ordered list, while a program
keeps them in records, tuples and lists. A _signature_ (`Sig a`) describes how a value of type `a`
corresponds to such a list, in both directions.

    Sig.pair (Sig.u8 (T.r2 batch pixels)) (Sig.u8 (T.r1 batch))

A signature is a list of _slots_, one per tensor in order, together with two functions: _build_
makes a value from tensors taken from the front of a list, one per slot, and _flatten_ lists a
value's tensors in slot order. Each slot carries a _label_, from which `Graph.build` names a graph's
inputs and outputs; a dtype and shape, which it may declare or leave open; and a role. Every slot
made here has the role `Fed` (`Graph.Role`): it is given with every run of a graph.

Everything rests on one contract that no type states, the _round trip_: given one tensor per slot,
_build_ makes a value whose _flatten_ gives those same tensors back, in the same order. It can
break, for example, where a record field's accessor reads a different field of the same type from
the one its constructor argument fills, or where `map` is given a `from` that does not undo `to`.
`Graph.build` checks the round trip of its input and output signatures and refuses a graph that
breaks it. Nothing else checks it.

A different mistake is to give `list n` a list whose length is not `n`: its _flatten_ can then
give more or fewer tensors than it has slots. `Graph.build` refuses a graph whose output gives, in
all, a different number of tensors from its signature's slots.

Building never fails. A tensor slot made here that finds the list empty builds an f32 scalar 0
instead, whatever type it declares.

The dtype and shape a slot declares are what `Graph.build` gives an input. For an output they are
not compared with the result: the graph takes them from the result itself.

Records are described as `elm/json` decoder pipelines are: `record` takes the constructor, and each
`field` supplies the next argument together with the accessor that reads it back.

aliases.name: Builder
aliases.comment:
A signature being put together, as an `elm/json` decoder pipeline is: it flattens an `r` and
builds an `f`.

`record` starts one with `f` the record's constructor, and each `field` supplies the constructor's
next argument. When every argument is supplied and the accessors read the record being built, `r`
and `f` are the same type and the builder is a `Sig` of it.

aliases.name: Sig
aliases.comment:
A signature for values of type `a`: the slots of the tensors one `a` holds, how to build an
`a` from them and how to flatten one back. The round trip, described at the top of this module, is
its contract, and only `Graph.build` checks it.

values.name: anyTensor
values.comment:
A signature for one tensor that declares no dtype and no shape.

`Graph.build` refuses it as a graph input, since an input needs both. As a graph output it is
accepted, and the output's dtype and shape are the result's. Its type admits any kind, dtype and
shape, and nothing checks the tensor it builds against them.
values.type: Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor k d s)

values.name: bf16
values.comment: Creates a signature for one bf16 tensor of the given shape.
values.type: Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.BF16 s)

values.name: f32
values.comment: Creates a signature for one f32 tensor of the given shape.
values.type: Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 s)

values.name: field
values.comment:
Adds the next field to a record signature, given the accessor that reads it and its
signature. Its slots follow those of the fields before it, and its built value is passed to the
constructor as the next argument.

Among other conditions, each accessor must read the field that its argument fills. The types
refuse a field of the wrong type but not one of the same type read from the wrong place, which can
break the round trip.
values.type: (r -> a) -> Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Builder r (a -> f) -> Signature.Builder r f

values.name: i64
values.comment:
Creates a signature for one signed 64-bit integer tensor of the given shape. Its dtype name,
as a graph's specs give it, is `si64`.
values.type: Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 s)

values.name: label
values.comment:
Returns the signature with every slot labelled `l`, replacing any label set inside it, so the
outermost `label` wins. A slot made by this module that no `label` reaches carries `arg`.

`Graph.build` makes the names of a graph's inputs and outputs from these labels, after replacing
`arg` with a default: `arg` for inputs, `result` for outputs. A label that one slot of the input (or
output) signature carries is then that slot's name. One that several carry is numbered, `l0`, `l1`
.., across the whole signature, not only within the part `label` was applied to.
values.type: String.String -> Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Sig a

values.name: list
values.comment:
Creates a signature for a list of `n` values of one signature, their slots one after another.

It builds exactly `n` values, none when `n` is 0 or less. It flattens every element of the list it
is given, however many, so a list whose length is not `n` can flatten to more or fewer tensors than
the signature has slots.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Sig (List.List a)

values.name: map
values.comment:
Creates a signature for `b` from one for `a`, with the same slots. Building applies `to` to the
value the signature for `a` builds, and flattening applies `from` first.

`from` must undo `to`. Where it does not, the round trip can break.
values.type: (a -> b) -> (b -> a) -> Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Sig b

values.name: mask
values.comment: Creates a signature for one mask, a tensor of dtype `bool`, of the given shape.
values.type: Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Mask s)

values.name: pair
values.comment:
Creates a signature for a pair, whose slots are the first signature's followed by the
second's.
values.type: Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Sig b -> Signature.Sig ( a, b )

values.name: record
values.comment:
Starts a record signature from the record's constructor. It has no slots until `field` adds
them, one field per constructor argument, in argument order.

    Sig.record Batch
        |> Sig.field .images (Sig.u8 (T.r2 batch pixels))
        |> Sig.field .labels (Sig.u8 (T.r1 batch))
values.type: f -> Signature.Builder r f

values.name: tensor
values.comment: Creates a signature for one tensor of the given dtype and shape.
values.type: Tensor.DType k d -> Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor k d s)

values.name: triple
values.comment: Creates a signature for a triple, whose slots are the three signatures' in order.
values.type: Signature.Sig a -> Signature.Sig b -> Signature.Sig c -> Signature.Sig ( a, b, c )

values.name: u8
values.comment:
Creates a signature for one unsigned 8-bit integer tensor of the given shape. Its dtype name,
as a graph's specs give it, is `ui8`.
values.type: Tensor.Shape s -> Signature.Sig (Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.U8 s)

values.name: unit
values.comment: A signature with no slots: it builds `()` and flattens nothing.
values.type: Signature.Sig ()

name: Tensor
comment:
Tensors are what a computation in this package is written with, and this module defines the
`Tensor` type, the types that go with it, and operations that make a new tensor from others.

A tensor is a description of a computation, not its elements. Making one works out its shape and
dtype, but computes no element values. Those are computed only when the tensor is run: by MAX,
given a `Graph` that `Graph.Max` writes out, or in plain Elm by `Tensor.Eval`, which runs a `Graph`,
or a tensor that reads no graph input.

A tensor's type, `Tensor kind dtype shape`, has three parameters. The _kind_ is the Elm type of its
elements, `Float` or `Int`. The dtype is a tag such as `F32` or `I64`. The shape is a _rank type_,
`R0` to `R5`, or the `Elems` described under Shapes. A rank type fixes the number of axes and gives
each a tag: `Tensor Float F32 (R2 Batch Hidden)` is a matrix of `f32` elements whose outer axis is
tagged `Batch`. An _axis tag_ is a type the user declares, such as `type Batch = Batch`, and names
an axis without giving its size. Mixing up axes, ranks, kinds or dtypes is therefore a compile
error, but sizes are not in the types: two `Dim Batch` values may hold different sizes.

Sizes are checked when each tensor is made instead. An operation that finds its operands do not fit,
in size or otherwise, still gives a tensor, but one carrying a _build error_: a message saying what
did not fit. Tensors built on it are marked as failed too. `Graph.build` can report build errors of
the tensors its outputs depend on, and `Tensor.Eval.floats`, `ints` and `mask` return those of the
tensor they are given. Index values are not checked this way: an index outside its axis, given to
`take`, `rowsAt`, `put` or `putAdd`, is not a build error, and `Tensor.Eval` refuses it when it
runs; `pick` gives 0 for one in a row of finite values.

An element-wise operation does no implicit broadcasting. Its operands must have one shape, except
that a scalar is spread over the other operand; an axis of size 1 is not stretched to match a
larger one. To add a vector to every row of a matrix, a _broadcast axis_ is made for the rows:
`broadcast`, `rows`, `columns` and `maskBroadcast` add an axis of size 1 whose size is not known
yet, and the next element-wise operation gives it its partner's size there, unless the partner is a
scalar or has a broadcast axis there too, when it stays a broadcast axis. A broadcast axis passes
unchanged through the element-wise functions of one tensor other than `sign`, and through
`transpose` and `permute`; `insertOne`, `dropOne` and the functions that make broadcast axes keep
those already there; and `matmul3` and `matmul4` treat one on a batch axis as an element-wise
operation does. Most other operations refuse a tensor with one, with a build error, and so does
`Graph.build` for an output that still has one. `shapeOf` reports a broadcast axis as 1, and the
constructors that copy another tensor's shape, such as `zerosLike`, make a real axis of size 1
there.

Functions take the tensor they act on last, so that a pipeline reads left to right. For a function
of two tensors that puts the second operand first: `x |> minus y` is x − y, and so is `minus y x`.
This holds for the arithmetic, the comparisons, `and`, `or` and `xor`, and the products, where
`x |> matmul w` is x @ w. `select` and `concat2` take their operands in reading order instead.

# Shapes

`One` is the tag that `one` and `insertOne` give a real axis of size 1, and `Elems` stands for a
shape that may be any.

# Dtypes

A tensor's kind is fixed by its dtype: `Float` for the floating-point dtypes
(`Tensor Float F32 s`) and `Int` for the integer ones (`Tensor Int I64 s`). The values given to
`int`, `constant`, `full`, `fromList`, `fullLikeInt` and `padInt` have that type, so an integer
given to them is kept as an `Int` and never converted to `Float`. In native code, where an `Int`
has 64 bits, every 64-bit value is therefore exact; under JavaScript an `Int` holds every integer
exactly only up to 2⁵³. An integer that `int8`, `int32` or `uint8` cannot hold, such as 300 for
`uint8`, is a build error; `int64` and `uint64` accept every `Int`.

A `uint64` element is the `Int` with the same 64 bits, so 2⁶³ … 2⁶⁴ − 1 are given and read as
negative `Int`s: `fromList uint64 (r1 n) [ -1 ]` holds 2⁶⁴ − 1.

aliases.name: Axis
aliases.comment:
One axis, named by its position and typed by the shape with the axis (`s`), the shape without it
(`r`) and the axis's tag (`c`).

The same value serves an operation that removes the axis, reading it as going from `s` to `r`
(`sum`, `argMax` and the other reductions), and one that inserts it, reading it backwards from `r`
to `s` (`broadcast`, `broadcastTo`, `insertOne`, `maskBroadcast`). Operations that keep the axis,
such as `softmax`, `cumsum`, `flip` and `sort`, use only its position. Values come from the
generated `Tensor.Axis`, such as `Axis.axis1of2` and `Axis.last2`.

aliases.name: BF16
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `bfloat16`: a 16-bit float with `f32`'s exponent range.

aliases.name: DType
aliases.comment:
An element type, typed by the Elm type of its elements and its dtype tag:
`float32 : DType Float F32`, `int64 : DType Int I64`. The values are `float16` .. `uint64`; there is
none for masks.

aliases.name: Dim
aliases.comment:
The size of one axis, typed by the axis's tag: `dim Hidden 128 : Dim Hidden`.

The size is a value, not part of the type, so two `Dim Hidden`s may hold different sizes, and
nothing requires a size to be positive. Sizes are compared when tensors are made.

aliases.name: Elems
aliases.comment:
A shape parameter standing for whatever shape a tensor has, so that one function can be applied
to every tensor of a model (`Optim.custom`, `Param.mapElems`). It is not a rank type, so only the
functions here that accept a tensor of any shape accept one typed with it.

aliases.name: F16
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `float16`: IEEE half precision.

aliases.name: F32
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `float32`: IEEE single precision.

aliases.name: F64
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `float64`: IEEE double precision.

aliases.name: I32
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `int32`: signed 32-bit integers.

aliases.name: I64
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `int64`: signed 64-bit integers.

aliases.name: I8
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `int8`: signed 8-bit integers.

aliases.name: Lift
aliases.comment:
A statement that shape `t` is shape `s` with a leading axis tagged `n` added in front. It names
no axis and holds nothing else: `stack` and `unstack` take one for its type alone. Values come from
the generated `Tensor.Axis` (`Axis.liftRank1`).

aliases.name: Mask
aliases.comment:
A tensor of booleans, with a shape type but no kind or dtype parameter. The comparisons,
`isInfinite` and `isNaN` make one, and `select`, `and`, `or`, `xor` and `not` take one; `indicator`
turns one into numbers.

aliases.name: One
aliases.comment:
The axis tag of a real axis of size 1, as `one` and `insertOne` make and `dropOne` removes.

The tag does not make an axis real: `broadcast`, `rows` and `columns` leave the tag of their new
axis free, so a broadcast axis may be tagged `One` too.

aliases.name: Perm
aliases.comment:
A reordering of the axes of shape `s` into shape `t`, made of swaps of two axes, as
`Tensor.Axis.swap01of2` and the like make and `Tensor.Axis.andThen` joins.

aliases.name: R0
aliases.comment: The rank type of a scalar, which has no axes.

aliases.name: R1
aliases.comment: The rank type of a vector, whose one axis is tagged `a`.

aliases.name: R2
aliases.comment: The rank type of a matrix, whose axes are tagged `a` and `b`, outermost first.

aliases.name: R3
aliases.comment: The rank type of a shape with three axes, tagged outermost first.

aliases.name: R4
aliases.comment: The rank type of a shape with four axes, tagged outermost first.

aliases.name: R5
aliases.comment: The rank type of a shape with five axes, tagged outermost first.
aliases.type: Tensor.Internal.Types.R5 a b c d e

aliases.name: Retag
aliases.comment:
One axis that an operation keeps in place but may resize, typed by two shapes that are the same
apart from that axis (`s` and `t`) and the axis's tag in each (`a` in `s`, `c` in `t`). `slice`,
`concat`, `pad`, `take` and `topK` take one, with a `Dim c` for the new size where they need it.
Values come from the generated `Tensor.Axis` (`Axis.retag1of2`).

aliases.name: Shape
aliases.comment:
The sizes of a tensor's axes, typed by a rank type and so by the number of axes and their tags:
`r2 batch hidden : Shape (R2 Batch Hidden)`. `scalar` and `r1` .. `r5` make one.

aliases.name: Tensor
aliases.comment:
A tensor: a description of a computation whose result has elements of the Elm type `e`
(`Float` or `Int`), the dtype `dtype` (`F32`, `I64` ..) and a shape typed by `shape`
(`R2 Batch Hidden`).

Making a tensor computes no elements, as the module documentation describes.

aliases.name: U64
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `uint64`: unsigned 64-bit integers.

aliases.name: U8
aliases.comment: The dtype tag of `uint8`: unsigned 8-bit integers.

values.name: abs
values.comment: Returns the absolute value of each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: acos
values.comment: Returns the arc cosine of each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: and
values.comment: Returns the mask of where both masks hold.
values.type: Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: arange
values.comment:
Returns the `int64` vector `start`, `start + step`, `start + 2 * step`, … with as many elements as
the size of `n`.
values.type: { start : Basics.Int, step : Basics.Int } -> Tensor.Dim n -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 (Tensor.R1 n)

values.name: argMax
values.comment:
Returns the position, along the axis `axis` names, of the largest element at each position of
the other axes.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 r

values.name: argMin
values.comment:
Returns the position, along the axis `axis` names, of the smallest element at each position of
the other axes.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 r

values.name: atLeast
values.comment: Returns the mask of where x >= y: `x |> atLeast y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: atMost
values.comment: Returns the mask of where x <= y: `x |> atMost y`. It is `atLeast` with its operands swapped.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: atanh
values.comment: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: bfloat16
values.comment: The dtype `bf16`, of `Float` elements.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float Tensor.BF16

values.name: bottomK
values.comment:
Returns the `k` smallest elements of `x` along the axis `retag` names, smallest first, and their
positions along that axis. Otherwise it is `topK`, with the same build errors and gradient and GPU
refusals.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> ( Tensor.Tensor k d t, Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 t )

values.name: broadcast
values.type: Tensor.Axis t s c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: broadcastTo
values.comment:
Returns `x` with a new axis of size `c` where `axis` names one, every slice along it a copy of
`x`. Unlike `broadcast`, it gives the axis its size at once. A broadcast axis already in `x` is a
build error.
values.type: Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Axis t s c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: cast
values.comment: Returns `x` with each element converted to the dtype `d`.
values.type: Tensor.DType k d -> Tensor.Tensor k0 d0 s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: castLike
values.comment:
Returns `x` with each element converted to the dtype of `y`, whose values are not used:
`x |> castLike y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d t -> Tensor.Tensor k0 d0 s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: chunks
values.comment:
Returns the consecutive slices of `size` elements of `x` along the axis `retag` names, in order.
When `size` is not positive or does not divide that axis's size, the result is instead a list of
one tensor, carrying a build error.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> List.List (Tensor.Tensor k d t)

values.name: columns
values.comment: Returns a matrix whose every column is the vector, the columns being a broadcast axis.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 a) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b)

values.name: concat
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Dim c -> List.List (Tensor.Tensor k d s) -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: concat2
values.comment:
Returns `x` followed by `y` along the axis `rx` names, in reading order rather than pipeline
order: `concat2 rx ry size x y`. `ry` only types `y`. `size` must be the total size along that axis,
a build error otherwise.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Retag u t b c -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d u -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: constant
values.comment:
Returns the scalar `v` of the dtype `d`, given in the dtype's kind: `constant bfloat16 0.5`,
`constant uint8 200`. An integer that the dtype cannot hold, such as 300 for `uint8`, is a build
error.
values.type: Tensor.DType e d -> e -> Tensor.Tensor e d Tensor.R0

values.name: cos
values.comment: Returns the cosine of each element, in radians.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: cumsum
values.comment:
Returns the running sums of `x` along the axis `axis` names, which is kept: each element is the
sum of the elements up to and including it.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: cumsumWith
values.comment:
Returns the running sums that `cumsum` returns, but with `exclusive` each element leaves itself
out of its sum, and with `reverse` the sums run from the end of the axis.
values.type: { exclusive : Basics.Bool, reverse : Basics.Bool } -> Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: dim
values.comment:
Returns a dimension of size `n` for the axis tag whose constructor is given:
`hidden = dim Hidden 128`. The constructor is used only for its type, and any `Int` is accepted as
the size, zero and negative included.
values.type: tag -> Basics.Int -> Tensor.Dim tag

values.name: dividedBy
values.comment: Returns x / y, element by element: `x |> dividedBy y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: dot
values.comment: Returns the inner product of two vectors, a scalar: `x |> dot y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 a) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 a) -> Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0

values.name: dropOne
values.comment:
Returns `x` without the axis `axis` names, which is meant to have size 1. Dropping an axis of
another size is a build error, unless `x` has no elements. A broadcast axis is dropped when `x` has
another broadcast axis, and is a build error when it is `x`'s only one.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r Tensor.One -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d r

values.name: dtypeName
values.comment:
Returns the name of `x`'s dtype, such as `"f32"`, `"bf16"`, `"si64"` or `"ui8"`: a signed
integer dtype's name starts `si` and an unsigned one's `ui`, unlike the names `int64` and `I64`. For
a tensor with a build error the dtype may be a stand-in, as for `shapeOf`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> String.String

values.name: equals
values.comment: Returns the mask of where x == y: `x |> equals y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: erf
values.comment: Returns the error function of each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: exp
values.comment: Returns e raised to each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: factorLast2
values.comment:
Returns the vector as a matrix of the sizes of `a` and `b`, filled row by row: the inverse of
`mergeLast2`. Sizes whose product is not the vector's size are a build error.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 m) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b)

values.name: factorLast3
values.comment:
Returns `x` with its last axis split, row-major, into two of the sizes of `a` and `b`: the
inverse of `mergeLast3`. Sizes whose product is not the last axis's size are a build error,
unless `x`'s first axis has size 0.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 x m) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 x a b)

values.name: factorLast4
values.comment:
Returns `x` with its last axis split, row-major, into two of the sizes of `a` and `b`: the
inverse of `mergeLast4`. Sizes whose product is not the last axis's size are a build error,
unless one of `x`'s first two axes has size 0.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 x y m) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 x y a b)

values.name: fillLike
values.comment:
Returns a tensor of `x`'s shape whose every element is the scalar `c`, which may be any scalar
tensor, not only a constant: `fillLike rate grad`. A broadcast axis of `x` is a real axis of size 1
in the result.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0 -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: flatten
values.comment:
Returns every element of `x`, in row-major order, along one axis of size `m`. A size other than
`x`'s number of elements is a build error.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 m)

values.name: flattenTail3
values.comment:
Returns `x` with everything after its first axis flattened, in row-major order, into one axis of
size `m`, such as a batch of images to a batch of vectors. A size other than the product of the
flattened axes' sizes is a build error, unless `x`'s first axis has size 0.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 n m)

values.name: flattenTail4
values.comment:
Returns what `flattenTail3` returns, for a tensor of rank 4, such as a batch of multi-channel
images.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 n a b c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 n m)

values.name: flip
values.comment: Returns `x` with its elements along the axis `axis` names in reverse order.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: float
values.comment: Returns the `f32` scalar `f`.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float Tensor.F32 Tensor.R0

values.name: float16
values.comment: The dtype `f16`, of `Float` elements.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float Tensor.F16

values.name: float32
values.comment: The dtype `f32`, of `Float` elements.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float Tensor.F32

values.name: float64
values.comment: The dtype `f64`, of `Float` elements.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Float Tensor.F64

values.name: floor
values.comment: Returns each element rounded down to a whole number.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: fromList
values.comment:
Returns the tensor of the dtype `d` and the shape `s` holding `values` in row-major order:
`fromList float32 (r1 three) [ 1, 2.5, 4 ]`, `fromList int64 (r1 two) [ 7, -3 ]`. A number of values
other than the number of elements of `s` is a build error, and so is an integer that the dtype
cannot hold.
values.type: Tensor.DType e d -> Tensor.Shape s -> List.List e -> Tensor.Tensor e d s

values.name: full
values.comment:
Returns a tensor of the dtype `d` and the shape `s` whose every element is `v`:
`full float32 0.5 (r2 batch hidden)`, `full int64 7 (r1 n)`. An integer that the dtype cannot hold
is a build error, as for `constant`.
values.type: Tensor.DType e d -> e -> Tensor.Shape s -> Tensor.Tensor e d s

values.name: fullLike
values.comment:
Returns a tensor of the floating-point `x`'s dtype and shape whose every element is `v`. A
broadcast axis of `x` is a real axis of size 1 in the result.
values.type: Basics.Float -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: fullLikeInt
values.comment:
Returns a tensor of the integer `x`'s dtype and shape whose every element is `v`, kept as an
`Int`. A `v` that the dtype cannot hold is a build error. A broadcast axis of `x` is a real axis of
size 1 in the result.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s

values.name: gelu
values.comment:
Returns x · Φ(x) of each element x, Φ being the standard normal distribution function: the
erf form of GELU.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: geluTanh
values.comment: Returns the GELU of each element by its tanh approximation.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: greaterThan
values.comment: Returns the mask of where x > y: `x |> greaterThan y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: hannWindow
values.comment:
Returns the Hann window of n points in the dtype `d`, n being the size of `n`: element i is
½ − ½ cos (2π i / N), where N is n when `periodic` and the larger of n − 1 and 1 otherwise.
values.type: { periodic : Basics.Bool } -> Tensor.DType Basics.Float d -> Tensor.Dim n -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d (Tensor.R1 n)

values.name: indicator
values.comment: Returns 1 where the mask holds and 0 where it does not, in the dtype `d`.
values.type: Tensor.DType k d -> Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: insertOne
values.comment:
Returns `x` with a new real axis of size 1, tagged `One`, where `axis` names one. Unlike the
axis `broadcast` adds, it keeps size 1.
values.type: Tensor.Axis t s Tensor.One -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: int
values.comment: Returns the `int64` scalar `n`, kept as an `Int` rather than converted to `Float`.
values.type: Basics.Int -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 Tensor.R0

values.name: int32
values.comment: The dtype `si32`, of `Int` elements from −2³¹ to 2³¹ − 1.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Int Tensor.I32

values.name: int64
values.comment: The dtype `si64`, of signed 64-bit `Int` elements.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Int Tensor.I64

values.name: int8
values.comment: The dtype `si8`, of `Int` elements from −128 to 127.
values.type: Tensor.DType Basics.Int Tensor.I8

values.name: iota
values.comment: Returns the `int64` vector 0, 1, … , n − 1, where n is the size of `n`.
values.type: Tensor.Dim n -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int Tensor.I64 (Tensor.R1 n)

values.name: isInfinite
values.comment: Returns the mask of where `x` is +∞ or −∞.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: isNaN
values.comment: Returns the mask of where `x` is NaN.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: lessThan
values.comment:
Returns the mask of where x < y: `x |> lessThan y`. It is `greaterThan` with its operands
swapped.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: log
values.comment: Returns the natural logarithm of each element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: log1p
values.comment: Returns log (1 + x) of each element x.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: logSoftmax
values.comment: Returns log (softmax x) along the axis `axis` names, which is kept.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: logSumExp
values.comment:
Returns log (sum (exp x)) along the axis `axis` names.

The largest element along the axis is subtracted before the exponentials and added back after the
log, which keeps the exponentials from overflowing. Where that largest element is +∞ or −∞, as
along an axis holding only −∞, the result is NaN.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d r

values.name: lowerTriangle
values.comment:
Returns the mask that is true on and below the main diagonal of a matrix of `x`'s shape, whose
values are not used: the causal mask. The type gives both axes one tag, which does not make their
sizes equal, and a matrix that is not square is accepted.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a a) -> Tensor.Mask (Tensor.R2 a a)

values.name: maskBroadcast
values.comment:
Returns the mask with a new broadcast axis where `axis` names one, as `broadcast` does for a
tensor.
values.type: Tensor.Axis t s c -> Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask t

values.name: matVec
values.comment: Returns the matrix–vector product m @ v: `m |> matVec v`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 a)

values.name: matmul
values.comment: Returns the matrix product x @ w: `x |> matmul w`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 b c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a c)

values.name: matmul3
values.comment:
Returns the product of each of the `n` matrices of `x` with the matching matrix of `w`:
`x |> matmul3 w`. A batch axis of size 1 in one operand takes the other's size, so `x` with one
matrix and `w` with five give five products.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n b c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n a c)

values.name: matmul3By2
values.comment:
Returns the product of each of the `n` matrices of `x` with the one matrix `w`:
`x |> matmul3By2 w`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 b c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 n a c)

values.name: matmul4
values.comment:
Returns the product of each matrix of `x` with the matching matrix of `w`, over two leading
batch axes: `x |> matmul4 w`. A batch axis of size 1 in one operand takes the other's size.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 m n b c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 m n a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 m n a c)

values.name: max
values.comment:
Returns the larger of x and y at each element: `x |> max y`. In `Tensor.Eval` a NaN operand is
ignored, so the result is NaN only where both are. `maximum` is the reduction along an axis.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: maximum
values.comment: Returns the largest elements of `x` along the axis `axis` names.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d r

values.name: maximumAll
values.comment: Returns the largest element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0

values.name: mean
values.comment: Returns the means of `x` along the axis `axis` names.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d r

values.name: meanAll
values.comment: Returns the mean of every element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d Tensor.R0

values.name: mergeLast2
values.comment:
Returns the matrix as a vector of size `m`, row by row: the inverse of `factorLast2`. A size
other than the matrix's number of elements is a build error.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 m)

values.name: mergeLast3
values.comment:
Returns `x` with its last two axes merged, row-major, into one of size `m`, such as heads ×
head size back to a model width: the inverse of `factorLast3`. A size other than the product of the
two axes' sizes is a build error, unless `x`'s first axis has size 0.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 x a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 x m)

values.name: mergeLast4
values.comment:
Returns `x` with its last two axes merged, row-major, into one of size `m`: the inverse of
`factorLast4`. A size other than the product of the two axes' sizes is a build error, unless one
of `x`'s first two axes has size 0.
values.type: Tensor.Dim m -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R4 x y a b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R3 x y m)

values.name: min
values.comment:
Returns the smaller of x and y at each element: `x |> min y`. In `Tensor.Eval` a NaN operand is
ignored, as for `max`. `minimum` is the reduction along an axis.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: minMax
values.comment: Returns the smallest and the largest element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> { min : Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0, max : Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0 }

values.name: minimum
values.comment: Returns the smallest elements of `x` along the axis `axis` names.
values.type: Tensor.Axis s r c -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d r

values.name: minimumAll
values.comment: Returns the smallest element.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d Tensor.R0

values.name: minus
values.comment: Returns x − y, element by element: `x |> minus y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: modBy
values.comment:
Returns the remainder of each element of `x` divided by the matching element of `m`:
`x |> modBy m`. In `Tensor.Eval` the remainder has the sign of `m`, as `Basics.modBy`'s does,
in native code `uint64` elements are divided as unsigned numbers, and a 0 anywhere in `m` stops
the run with an error.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s

values.name: negate
values.comment:
Returns each element negated. For `uint8` and `uint64` tensors it is a build error, because the
package's record of what MAX compiles lists it as refused for them.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: not
values.comment: Returns the mask of where the mask does not hold.
values.type: Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: notEquals
values.comment: Returns the mask of where x /= y: `x |> notEquals y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: one
values.comment: The dimension of a real axis of size 1, tagged `One`, such as a grey image's channel axis.
values.type: Tensor.Dim Tensor.One

values.name: ones
values.comment: Returns a tensor of the dtype and shape given whose every element is 1.
values.type: Tensor.DType e d -> Tensor.Shape s -> Tensor.Tensor e d s

values.name: onesLike
values.comment:
Returns a tensor of `x`'s dtype and shape whose every element is 1. A broadcast axis of `x` is a
real axis of size 1 in the result.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: or
values.comment: Returns the mask of where either mask holds.
values.type: Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask s -> Tensor.Mask s

values.name: outer
values.comment: Returns the outer product of two vectors, whose element (i, j) is x[i] · y[j]: `x |> outer y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 a) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b)

values.name: pad
values.comment:
Returns `x` with `before` elements added before it and `after` after it along the axis `retag`
names, each `value`. `size` must be the padded size, and neither count may be negative; each is a
build error otherwise.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> { before : Basics.Int, after : Basics.Int, value : Basics.Float } -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d t

values.name: padInt
values.comment:
Returns what `pad` returns, for an integer tensor, with the fill `value` kept as an `Int`. A fill
that the dtype cannot hold is a build error, even when both counts are 0.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> { before : Basics.Int, after : Basics.Int, value : Basics.Int } -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int d t

values.name: permute
values.comment: Returns `x` with its axes reordered as `perm` says: `x |> permute Axis.swap12of4`.
values.type: Tensor.Perm s t -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: pick
values.comment:
Returns one element of each row of `x`, the one at column `indices[i]` of row i:
`x |> pick indices`.

It multiplies each row by a row that is 1 at the picked column and 0 elsewhere, and sums. So an
index outside 0 … c − 1 gives 0 for a row of finite values, with no error, and a NaN anywhere in a
row, or ±∞ anywhere but at the picked column, makes that row's result NaN.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int i (Tensor.R1 n) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 n c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 n)

values.name: plus
values.comment: Returns x + y, element by element: `x |> plus y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: pow
values.comment: Returns x raised to the power y, element by element: `x |> pow y`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: put
values.comment:
Returns `x` with its slices along the axis `retag` names at the positions in `indices` replaced
by the slices of `updates`, in order: `x |> put retag indices updates`. An index outside the axis
is not a build error; `Tensor.Eval` refuses it when it runs.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int i (Tensor.R1 c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d t -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: putAdd
values.comment:
Returns what `put` returns, but with each slice of `updates` added to the slice of `x` at its
index instead of replacing it, so that the updates at a repeated index add up.
values.type: Tensor.Retag s t a c -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Int i (Tensor.R1 c) -> Tensor.Tensor k d t -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: quickGelu
values.comment: Returns x · sigmoid (1.702 x) of each element x, an approximation of `gelu`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: r1
values.comment: Returns the vector shape of one dimension: `r1 hidden`.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Shape (Tensor.R1 a)

values.name: r2
values.comment: Returns the matrix shape of two dimensions, outermost first: `r2 batch hidden`.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Shape (Tensor.R2 a b)

values.name: r3
values.comment: Returns the shape of three dimensions, outermost first.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Shape (Tensor.R3 a b c)

values.name: r4
values.comment: Returns the shape of four dimensions, outermost first.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Dim d -> Tensor.Shape (Tensor.R4 a b c d)

values.name: r5
values.comment: Returns the shape of five dimensions, outermost first.
values.type: Tensor.Dim a -> Tensor.Dim b -> Tensor.Dim c -> Tensor.Dim d -> Tensor.Dim e -> Tensor.Shape (Tensor.R5 a b c d e)

values.name: relu
values.comment: Returns each element, or 0 where it is below 0.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d s

values.name: reshape
values.comment:
Returns `x`'s elements, in row-major order, in the shape `t`. A number of elements other than
`x`'s is a build error, and so is a broadcast axis in `x`.
values.type: Tensor.Shape t -> Tensor.Tensor k d s -> Tensor.Tensor k d t

values.name: round
values.comment:
Returns each element rounded to the nearest whole number. In `Tensor.Eval` a value halfway
between two goes to the even one.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s -> Tensor.Tensor Basics.Float d s

values.name: rows
values.comment:
Returns a matrix whose every row is the vector, the rows being a broadcast axis:
`x |> plus (rows bias)`.
values.type: Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R1 b) -> Tensor.Tensor k d (Tensor.R2 a b)

values.name: rowsAt
values.comment:
Returns the rows of the matrix at the positions in `ids`, in their order, as an embedding lookup
does: `table |> rowsAt ids`. An index outside the matrix is not a build error; `Tensor.Eval` refuses
it when it runs.
